Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Monday conducted searches at the residence of Trinamool Congress Rajya Sabha MP Nadimul Haque and six other premises across Delhi, West Bengal and Jharkhand. The move comes as part of a money laundering investigation linked to Urdu newspaper Akhbar-E-Mashriq.The searches, which began early Monday, were carried out by the ED's Kolkata zonal office in Kolkata, Delhi and Ranchi in connection with a case against Akhbar-E-Mashriq Pvt Ltd and its director Mohd Nadimul Haque. The operation was conducted in coordination with security forces and the state police forces concerned.According to officials, the Enforcement Case Information Report (ECIR) was registered after an FIR was filed by the Bidhannagar Police Commissionerate in West Bengal.The case involves "allegations concerning publication and dissemination of material promoting communal disharmony and also contains allegations regarding illegal transactions, unaccounted cash transactions and funding from suspicious sources."The agency is examining the financial dealings of the newspaper, Haque and other entities and individuals named in the case to trace the alleged proceeds of crime and establish the money trail.During the searches, ED teams are collecting documentary and digital evidence as part of the investigation under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA).The searches were still underway at the premises on Monday, with further details on any evidence recovered and the agency's next course of action awaited.The action forms part of the ED's broader investigations into cases where alleged proceeds of crime are suspected to have been generated or routed through financial transactions involving individuals or entities under investigation.
Article Summary: The Enforcement Directorate (ED) conducted searches at the residence of Trinamool Congress Rajya Sabha MP Nadimul Haque. The move comes as part of a money laundering investigation linked to Urdu newspaper Akhbar-E-Mashriq. The action forms part of the ED's broader investigations into cases where alleged proceeds of crime are suspected.

NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday hailed India-France relations, saying that the strategic partnership between the two countries is particularly special because it rests on the solid foundation of long-standing cultural and political ties.Addressing the inauguration of the Swaminarayan temple in Paris, Modi hoped that the grand temple would stand for centuries as a symbol of cooperation and opportunity between the two nations.“In recent years, relations between India and France have reached new heights. Together with my friend, President (Emmanuel) Macron, both nations are building a Special Global Strategic Partnership,” he said.The Prime Minister said the inauguration was more than a religious or architectural occasion, asserting that it embodied the spirit of universal brotherhood and the ancient Indian philosophy of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam.“Today, this stage has become an awakened platform for the spirit of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam,” he said. PM Modi also underlined that the establishment of temples and the spread of India's spiritual traditions overseas also carry with them the country's philosophical message of human unity. Referring to the ideal that minds should be united and hearts connected, he said India's civilisational thought has a universal appeal.PM Modi also placed the inauguration in the wider context of the rapidly expanding India-France partnership, noting that New Delhi and Paris were working together to build what he described as a Special Global Strategic Partnership.“We are also celebrating 2026 as the India-France Year of Innovation. This strategic partnership is particularly special because it rests on the solid foundation of our long-standing cultural and political ties,” he said.“Both countries are building a Special Global Strategic Partnership together,” he said, while recalling his cooperation with French President Emmanuel Macron.PM Modi said history bears witness that the sacrifice of Indian soldiers in France remains alive in the hearts of people to this day.“Language enthusiasts also know the pivotal role French scholars played in popularising Sanskrit. Romain Rolland’s writings on Ramakrishna Paramahamsa and Swami Vivekananda brought our societies closer,” he said.

Addressing the inauguration of the Swaminarayan temple in Paris, Modi hoped that the grand temple would stand for centuries as a symbol of cooperation and opportunity.

Article Title: Watch: CCTV captures moment Delhi's Satya Niketan building collapsed, leaving 6 dead
Article Text:
The CCTV footage showed the building suddenly giving way, sending debris crashing onto the road

10 patients taken to Trauma Centre

MCD orders demolition of dangerous building

NEW DELHI: CCTV footage has captured the moment a multi-storey building collapsed in Delhi's Satya Niketan area, killing six people and triggering a major rescue operation.The building, which housed a boys' paying guest accommodation near Delhi University's South Campus, collapsed around 1.30 pm on Sunday while repair and construction work was underway. The death toll rose to six after one more person rescued during the night was declared dead.The CCTV footage showed the building suddenly giving way, sending debris crashing onto the road. Rescue and search operations continued through the night as teams searched the rubble for anyone who may still be trapped.Multiple agencies, including the Delhi Police, Delhi Fire Service, National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and Delhi Disaster Management Authority, have been involved in the operation."One more person was rescued during the night but was brought dead, taking the toll to six," Deputy Commissioner of Police (Southwest) Amit Goel said, PTI reported.Police have registered a case against the building owner and others, while a magisterial inquiry has also been ordered. Officials are continuing efforts to trace people allegedly connected with the incident.To the residents, the collapse felt like a quake. “We felt the ground shake.When we ran outside, we saw that a house had completely collapsed,” said Roshan Pal, a student from Lucknow.“When I came out, a cloud of dust was spreading in all directions. That’s when we realised that the building had collapsed. We started removing one part of a wall soon after. Seven students were under it,” said Rahul Gaur, a resident, TOI reported.According to AIIMS, the JPN Apex Trauma Centre received 10 patients injured in the building collapse. Of the 10 patients, five were brought dead, while another patient who was in critical condition later succumbed to injuries.Three patients have been admitted and are undergoing treatment. One of them underwent limb surgery, while another patient with minor injuries was discharged after observation.Investigators are examining whether construction work carried out in the basement may have contributed to the collapse.Initial inquiries suggested that the basement was prone to waterlogging, which may have weakened the structure. Investigators are now examining whether construction work aggravated the situation and contributed to the collapse.The MCD is also looking into the matter. Similar concerns over basement work, water accumulation and the structural condition of the building have emerged in the preliminary probe.Police are likely to examine whether permission had been obtained for the work and why construction was being carried out during the monsoon, sources said. "The building owner, contractor and labourers will be interrogated," an investigator said, TOI reported.It was not immediately clear whether the building owner had obtained permission for the construction or whether the work was being carried out illegally, allegedly in connivance with local authorities.According to the MCD, the premises of Building/House No. 13, Satya Niketan, New Delhi, was found to be in a "ruinous, dangerous condition" and posed a threat to people occupying, visiting or passing by the building as well as those in the neighbourhood.Under Section 348 of the DMC Act, 1957, read with Section 491 of the Act, the MCD has ordered the property to be demolished within three days of receipt of the order.The order said that if the owner fails to comply within the specified period, the MCD will demolish the building and recover the demolition charges as arrears of tax.The collapse has raised fresh questions over the safety of buildings being used as paying guest accommodations and the enforcement of construction and fire safety norms in densely populated areas of Delhi.Congress leader and AICC Uttarakhand in-charge Kumari Selja questioned the BJP government over the safety of students living in such accommodations.“What is the BJP government doing? They have forgotten what happened at the coaching centre. A mafia is operating in Delhi. These children are sent away with so many hopes. They are the only support for their parents. Who is responsible for their safety?” Selja said.Former Delhi chief secretary Omesh Saigal said the incident should not be viewed in isolation and raised concerns over unauthorised construction in parts of the capital."Look at the kind of buildings constructed in Delhi—I would say that in some areas, one in five buildings is unauthorised; either the blueprints weren't approved, extra floors were added, or the construction is substandard," he said.Saigal also called for restrictions on new construction in areas that are already overcrowded. "At the very least, we should ban new construction in these areas. We must halt new construction or stop sanctioning building plans, for areas that are already over-congested and over-built. These are the things that need to be addressed," he added.
Article Summary: CCTV footage shows the building suddenly giving way, sending debris crashing onto the road. Rescue and search operations continued through the night as teams searched the rubble for anyone who may still be trapped. Police have registered a case against the building owner and others, while a magisterial inquiry has been ordered.

NEW DELHI: The death toll in the Satya Niketan building collapse in Delhi rose to six as search and rescue operations continued at the site, with teams clearing heavy debris and looking for any remaining trapped persons. Hours after the building collapse in a student-dominated area near Delhi University’s South Campus, the MCD has ordered action against illegal buildings with four or more storeys.One more body was recovered during late-night operations, taking the total number of fatalities to six.Teams from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF), Delhi Fire Service, Delhi Police and other agencies continued rescue operations at the site as they worked to remove the debris.The collapse that took place on Sunday afternoon, has raised fresh questions over the safety of buildings being used as paying guest (PG) accommodations and the enforcement of construction and fire safety norms in densely populated parts of the national capital.The Rekha Gupta-led Delhi government has ordered a magisterial inquiry into the incident and directed that an FIR be registered against the building owner, the chief minister’s office (CMO) said.The decision was taken following an on-site review and a preliminary assessment of the incident, the CMO said.“Following an on-site review and based on the preliminary assessment, the chief minister has ordered a Magisterial Inquiry of the incident and an FIR against the building owner,” the CMO said.It added that those found responsible for the incident would be held fully accountable and face the strictest provisions of the law.Meanwhile, Congress leader and AICC Uttarakhand in-charge Kumari Selja questioned the BJP government over the safety of students living in such accommodations. She said students are sent to Delhi with hopes of building their future and questioned who would be held responsible for their safety.“What is the BJP government doing? They have forgotten what happened at the coaching centre. A mafia is operating in Delhi. These children are sent away with so many hopes. They are the only support for their parents. Who is responsible for their safety?” Selja said.Former Delhi chief secretary Omesh Saigal said the incident should not be viewed as an isolated case, claiming that similar incidents occur every few months. He also raised concerns over unauthorised construction in parts of Delhi.Saigal alleged that some buildings either have unapproved blueprints, additional floors added later or substandard construction, and questioned whether authorities responsible for approving building plans had adequately checked their safety."Look at the kind of buildings constructed in Delhi - I would say that in some areas, one in five buildings is unauthorised; either the blueprints weren't approved, extra floors were added, or the construction is substandard," he said.He also called for restrictions on new construction in areas that are already overcrowded and over-built, saying authorities should consider stopping the sanctioning of new building plans in such areas and examine the safety of existing structures."At the very least, we should ban new construction in these areas. We must halt new construction—or stop sanctioning building plans—for areas that are already over-congested and over-built. These are the things that need to be addressed," he added.NSUI President Vinod Jakhar described the situation as extremely grave and said rescue operations were continuing under difficult conditions."Rescue operations are ongoing, and conditions are dire. Almost all the students being pulled out are dead. We tried our best to get those students out; we actually succeeded in rescuing about three of them. Had the medical facilities, medical teams, police, and fire brigade arrived on time—had all necessary resources and responsible officials been present promptly—perhaps more students could have been saved. But the BJP has no disaster management plan. Just look at how the country's Home Minister inaugurates a grand BJP office in Goa today, while here, a building collapses. BJP offices never collapse because they are built using money extorted from PG and coaching centre operators. Our only demand is justice for the students. Several of our colleagues have also sustained serious injuries. There is absolutely no accountability," Jakhar told news agency ANI.Meanwhile, Delhi Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha president Rajat Choudhary said the situation remained serious and appealed for speedy rescue efforts. He said ambulances and doctors were present in large numbers and urged both the Delhi and Central governments to ensure that those trapped were rescued quickly.Choudhary also appealed to political parties to avoid politicising the tragedy and instead extend support to the affected families and those involved in the rescue operation."This is not the time for politics; those affected were someone's children. Instead of playing politics, one should offer support. The opposition should not do this; they should stand in solidarity," he said.In a separate response, the Municipal Corporation of Delhi (MCD) ordered the immediate sealing of all illegal constructions with more than four floors and warned of strict action against officials found responsible.“All illegal constructions with more than four floors will be immediately sealed, and strict action will be taken against the guilty officials, leading to their immediate dismissal. These orders will be implemented with immediate effect,” the MCD said.
Article Summary: Death toll in Satya Niketan building collapse in Delhi rises to six. MCD orders action against illegal buildings with four or more storeys. Delhi government orders magisterial inquiry into the incident and an FIR against the building owner. Congress leader questions the safety of students living in such accommodations.

Article Title: 'Cracked skull' wasn't all: In eye of storm, 'influencer' Swatantra Bhardwaj
Article Text:
Swatantra Bhardwaj, 22, was detained in Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr district.

A provocative online presence

The hunt for Bhardwaj

(With inputs from PTI)

Poll Vote & Share your view Is the government doing enough to hold influencers accountable for their actions online? Yes, they are taking action No, they need to do more 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: Long before the viral video in which he boasted about assaulting a Jantar Mantar protester’s father, 'influencer' Swatantra Bhardwaj had built a sizeable following through provocative posts, political associations and incendiary remarks.Bhardwaj, 22, was detained in Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr district on Friday, hours after Delhi Police assured protesters from the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) that he would be arrested within 72 hours.Bhardwaj is accused of assaulting the father of student activist Nishu Azad during a protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on July 20.His detention came after a clip from an interview went viral in which Bhardwaj is heard claiming that he had "cracked the skull" of the father."Do you know which section this crime attracts? Section 307. He needed 60 stitches. The man was being taken away in an ambulance in serious condition. His daughter was standing outside the police station and saying that she would die by suicide if her father didn't get justice."But I was not even jailed. The world should know this. I was out and about through the night," Bhardwaj is heard saying in the video.He then named several political leaders while explaining why, according to him, he had little reason to fear arrest."I have the blessings of Hanuman upon me. And secondly, Kapil Mishra is my elder brother. They say Kapil Mishra called and I was released. Chirag Paswan is my elder brother. How many leaders do you know? Do you know Modi ji? Modi ji is also my elder brother. I have everyone's support," he claimed.There is, however, no evidence to establish that any of the political leaders named by Bhardwaj intervened on his behalf in the case.The viral clip also brought renewed attention to Bhardwaj's older social media posts and videos.According to news agency PTI, his Facebook page, which has around 327,000 followers, contains posts focused on cow protection, attacks on Muslims and critics of the government, as well as photographs appearing to show his proximity to political figures and official events.Some older videos circulating on social media purportedly show him making inflammatory remarks about Muslims and government critics. In others, he boasts about his political connections and claims he does not fear arrest.His online presence suggests that the persona seen in the viral clip was not an isolated episode, but part of a broader public image he had cultivated over time.On Thursday, a day before his detention, Bhardwaj shared a screenshot showing his name among the trends on X, captioning it, "Love you all Virodhi".He also posted a photograph on Instagram showing a 'kada' on his wrist with the caption "Feel the power!". The post appeared to reference a Delhi Police statement that Kumar had been injured by a 'kada' and "not by any weapon".His social media accounts also featured photographs with political leaders, including Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, Delhi minister Kapil Mishra and Union minister Chirag Paswan.Paswan said on Friday that Bhardwaj had misused his name and the names of other leaders.The Union minister for food processing industries said he had lodged a complaint against Bhardwaj and demanded action against him."No action despite the accused admitting to an attack that could have been fatal sets a bad example; I take responsibility for ensuring justice for the family," Paswan said.Bhardwaj's accounts also included what appeared to be AI-generated images of him with women wearing burqas or hijabs.One particularly violent image, posted on 22 May, showed Bhardwaj holding the bloodied chin of a man. The accompanying text referred to "Mughal" and included the words "aa gaya swad".His Instagram account, which had around 184,000 followers, was deactivated on Friday. He also has a verified account on X with more than 6,400 followers.The viral video intensified demands for action against Bhardwaj, with protesters raising the issue during the CJP demonstration in Delhi on Friday.Police subsequently deployed several teams to trace him.According to police officials, Bhardwaj had travelled to Bulandshahr and was staying in Naithla village. He allegedly fled the village on a motorcycle towards Khurja before a police team could apprehend him.He was wearing a helmet, apparently in an attempt to conceal his identity, police said.Local residents told TOI that Bhardwaj had arrived in Bulandshahr early on Friday, allegedly to evade arrest, and had taken shelter at the home of a local family.While there, he interacted with some journalists and reportedly repeated his claims about the alleged assault during the CJP protest.Bhardwaj was staying at the house of Harishankar Sharma, a Naithla resident who works as a cab driver in the Delhi-NCR region.Sharma said he had met Bhardwaj during an earlier journey.“Bhardwaj called me and said he wanted to come to my house to meet me. He arrived early in the morning along with another man. Initially, I did not suspect anything. But when media persons started arriving at my village, I sensed something was wrong,” Sharma said.Sharma said Bhardwaj later asked to borrow his motorcycle, saying he would return “within five minutes”.“Then I came to know that Delhi Police had detained him. It was only after that I learnt that he was wanted in a criminal case in the national capital. I still do not know much about the case,” Sharma said.The detention came after CJP representatives said Delhi Police had assured them that Bhardwaj “will be arrested within 72 hours”.The case has since drawn attention not only to the alleged assault but also to the online persona Bhardwaj had built through provocative posts, political associations and claims of influence.
Article Summary: Swatantra Bhardwaj, 22, was detained in Uttar Pradesh's Bulandshahr district on Friday. He is accused of assaulting the father of student activist Nishu Azad during a protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi on July 20. His detention came after a clip from an interview went viral in which he claimed he had "cracked the skull" of the father.

Article Title: Amazon techie leaves Rs 46 lakh package to join Indian Army, set to be commissioned at OTA Gaya
Article Text:
Shardendu Tiwari





LUCKNOW: Lucknow’s 27-year-old Shardendu Tiwari, who worked as a cloud engineer at Amazon with an annual package of around Rs 46 lakh, is set to be commissioned into the Army at the Officers Training Academy (OTA), Gaya, on Saturday.A second-generation soldier, Shardendu chose military service after leaving behind a corporate career and an opportunity with global aerospace company Airbus. His commissioning will mark the culmination of his journey from the technology sector to the armed forces.Shardendu resides in Neelmatha, Lucknow, and his family traces its roots to Pipergaon in Sultanpur district. His father, Honorary Captain Raj Kumar Tiwari, served in the Army Service Corps for 36 years before retiring. Inspired by his father, Shardendu developed an inclination towards joining the armed forces during his childhood.He completed his schooling at Kendriya Vidyalaya, Chandimandir, Haryana. He pursued a Bachelor of Engineering degree in Information Technology and later completed an MTech in Computer Science and Information Security from Punjab Engineering College, Chandigarh.Shardendu appeared for Army selection eight times before succeeding.He joined through the technical entry route, which enabled him to serve in the Army while remaining connected with technology.“I was also drawn to the armed forces because of the opportunities they offer for adventure and field service,” he said.During training at OTA Gaya, his leadership qualities earned him the appointment of Senior Under Officer (SUO), one of the highest cadet appointments at the academy. He enjoys playing basketball and table tennis.
Article Summary: Shardendu Tiwari, 27, is set to be commissioned into the Army at the Officers Training Academy (OTA), Gaya, on Saturday. His commissioning will mark the culmination of his journey from the technology sector to the armed forces. Article Title: 5 poll-bound states set to vote in February-March
Article Text:
5 poll bound states to vote in Feb-March

UP will vote almost 2 months before House term expires

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The advancement of Census in the four poll-bound states of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab and Goa - coupled with deferment of first phase of Census in the fifth poll-bound state of Manipur - has essentially cemented the schedule for the next round of assembly elections in the five states to Feb-March next year.Among the five states, the term of the Manipur assembly is expiring the earliest - on March 13, 2027. The term of Goa assembly ends March 14, 2027; Punjab assembly on March 16; Uttarakhand on March 28; and Uttar Pradesh only on May 22. All five had gone to polls together in 2022, but the first sitting of the UP assembly was on May 22, 2022.Since 2027 polls in these states will also be simultaneous, Election Commission is likely to take the conventional route of winding up polls before the earliest assembly expiry date - March 13.Thus, the UP polls would be held almost two months before the date of expiry of its assembly. This is in keeping with the pattern of the last three polls. EC's constitutional mandate allows it to hold a state poll anytime within six months prior to the expiry of its assembly's term.Given that a large and populous state like UP is almost certain to have multi-phase polling - though with fewer phases, going by the precedent set by EC in Bihar and West Bengal - polling could start in Feb or even in the beginning of March in case EC decides to restrict polls to two phases, like in Bihar.The poll announcement may come in Jan 2027.Since SIR has already been completed in three poll-bound states and is under way in the other two, EC is unlikely to go for annual summary revision there ahead of announcing assembly polls. At the end of SIR, the electorate in UP stood at 13.4 crore (decline of 13.2%), in Goa 10.6 lakh (10.2% less) and in Manipur 19.3 lakh (7.6% fall). The final rolls for Punjab and Uttarakhand will be published over the next couple of months.Centre had yesterday notified its decision to advance the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, non-snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand and Goa, to the period between Dec 1, 2026, and Jan 4, 2027, with Jan 5 as the reference date. It also notified the deferment of the houselisting phase of Census in Manipur.The advancing of the population enumeration phase in the four other poll-bound states will avert the logistical challenges that would have arisen on account of a clash between the usual timeline for Census and the assembly elections. Both elections and Census rely on the same pool of govt employees - largely teachers - for their conduct.Conventionally, the second phase of Census is held countrywide in Feb, with March 1 as the reference date.
Article Summary: The term of the Manipur assembly is expiring the earliest - on March 13, 2027. Election Commission is likely to take the conventional route of winding up polls before the earliest assembly expiry date. All five had gone to polls together in 2022, but the first sitting of the UP assembly was on May 22, 2022.

NEW DELHI: After endorsing a UN General Assembly resolution on equal-area world map, the govt warned Sunday that the proposed new map must depict India's sovereign territory, including the Union territories of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh, in accordance with India's official map and any inaccurate or misleading depiction would be unacceptable."Our position on India's sovereignty and territorial integrity is clear, consistent and non-negotiable," said MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal, replying to media queries.India was among the 164 countries that voted in favour of UN General Assembly's Sept 4 resolution, "Correct the Map: Rebalancing Global Cartographic Representation and Promoting Equitable Representation of the World's Regions, Particularly Africa".MEA said the resolution's purpose is to encourage the use of equal-area map projections that preserve the relative sizes of continental landmasses, and it neither adopts nor authenticates any particular world map, nor does it address political cartography, including international boundaries, disputed territories or place names."India voted in favour of the resolution and also made an explanation, stressing the underlying principle of promoting equal-area cartographic representation.We also highlighted that the resolution does not constitute endorsement of any specific map, projection or depiction of national boundaries," said Randhir Jaiswal.The resolution received abstentions from Estonia, Georgia, Lithuania, Moldova, Serbia and Ukraine, and a lone vote against it from US.The resolution noted that the Mercator projection remains widely used in educational, media, digital and official materials, despite the considerable distortion of landmasses to the North and South, far from the equator.It expressed concern that this distortion contributed to minimising the perceived sizes of Africa, Latin America and South Asia, and perpetuating an unbalanced view of the world. India welcomed the intention behind the resolution to promote more accurate and representative cartographic practices.

Article Text:

Delhi’s real test: Preparing before the next flood

A year after the Yamuna inundated large parts of Delhi, the river is again flowing above the danger mark. The immediate threat may be lower this time, but heavy rain in the upper catchment could quickly change the picture, exposing how vulnerable the city’s floodplain still remains.That vulnerability is built into Delhi’s geography. Every monsoon, as September sets in, the city watches the Yamuna closely because even a sharp rise in the river or a sudden surge in upstream discharge can quickly put thousands living and working along the floodplains at risk.The danger mark at the Old Iron Railway Bridge is 205.33 metres, while evacuation of vulnerable residents begins when the river reaches around 206 metres. On September 6, the Yamuna was flowing at 205.59 metres, already slightly above the danger mark.And it is not just the people living along the river who feel the impact. When the Yamuna rises sharply, critical roads and infrastructure can also be affected. The Loha Pul, a vital link between Central Delhi (including Kashmere Gate and Old Delhi Railway Station) and East Delhi, is among the key crossings vulnerable to rising waters during severe floods.Last year, the warning turned into a full-blown crisis.The Yamuna crossed the danger mark and rose above 207 metres, inundating several low-lying parts of the Capital and forcing more than 10,000 people to evacuate vulnerable areas.The impact extended well beyond flooded homes. Roads and public infrastructure were affected, electricity supplies were disrupted and houses were left covered in mud and silt after the water receded. Thousands whose livelihoods depended on the floodplain also took a hit.Floodwaters reached the Ring Road and Outer Ring Road, disrupting traffic between Majnu ka Tilla and the Salimgarh bypass. The Municipal Corporation of Delhi stopped cremations at Nigambodh Ghat and the Geeta Colony ground because of flooding. Water-treatment infrastructure was also affected.A major factor was the enormous volume of water released from the Hathnikund Barrage in Haryana after intense rainfall in the upper Yamuna catchment.A year later, attention is once again turning to the Yamuna.The monsoon remains active, with heavy rain reported in parts of Delhi and northern India. The immediate concern is not simply the river’s current level, but how much water is being released upstream and whether intense rainfall in the catchment pushes those levels sharply higher.The Yamuna has remained comparatively stable this year, despite crossing the danger mark.Dr Shiv Singh Rawat, water expert and convener of the WalkForYamuna Campaign, said the difference becomes clearer when the upstream discharge is examined. “This year’s situation needs to be understood in its proper hydrological context. The maximum discharge released from Hathnikund Barrage during this year was around 64,000 cusecs, which is significantly below an extreme flood situation. That helps explain why Delhi experienced a much less severe river-flood situation than in 2025. ”But that relative stability offers no guarantee.The India Meteorological Department has warned of isolated heavy rainfall over Haryana, Chandigarh and Delhi from September 10-12.Fairly widespread rain, accompanied by thunderstorms and lightning, is also likely over Uttarakhand from September 6-12, while rainfall disturbances are expected over Himachal Pradesh.For Delhi, what happens upstream can matter as much as what happens within the Capital itself.A spell of intense rainfall in the upper catchment can send a surge downstream, leaving communities along the floodplain with limited time to respond.The relatively stable Yamuna this year may have given Delhi a temporary reprieve, but the underlying vulnerability remains.The floodplain is not simply vacant land beside the river.It acts as a natural buffer during floods, helps recharge groundwater and performs an important ecological function.“The 2-km-stretch on both sides of Yamuna acts as a buffer for floods, restores groundwater balance and acts as an organic filter. However, excess rain will create flooding in Delhi, and sanitation is not adequate to handle floods in the Capital,” says environmentalist Kavita Ashok.Rawat warns that the greater danger could emerge gradually through construction and development. “The concern is that areas outside the most restrictive floodplain zones could gradually become corridors for permanent construction, infrastructure and commercial riverfront activity,” he says. “That would undermine the very floodplain functions that protect the city.”The question, therefore, is not only whether the Yamuna will rise this September. It is whether Delhi is becoming more or less vulnerable when it does.For families living along Delhi’s floodplain, the monsoon is not simply a season of heavy rain. It is a recurring threat of displacement.When the river rises, families may have to move their belongings, livestock and essentials to higher ground with little warning.The granddaughter of Ramu Sahni, who lives with his family near the Yamuna floodplain, told TOI that residents don’t receive any advance warning.“We receive no warning on time. We see the rise in the water level of Yamuna and ourselves decide to shift to the roads with all our belongings. The authorities then notice the crowd on the roads and help us with tents.”Sahni, who came to Delhi from Bihar in search of employment many years ago, says the relief arrangements have also changed. “Earlier, they used to provide us with some ration and water in tents but now the situation has changed,” he says. “I don’t live here for free, I pay rent.”For many residents, simply relocating permanently is not an easy option.Their lives are tied to the floodplain through work, transport, markets and social networks. When the water recedes, they return.“We return back here when the water recedes after 2 months. This is all we have. I run a rickshaw, we are mostly ragpickers. Where will we go?”That cycle of evacuation, waiting, returning and rebuilding has become part of life for many families.For families with livestock, evacuation is even more complicated.Leaving home is one thing. Moving buffaloes, cattle, calves and other animals to safety is another. Stray animals are even more vulnerable, particularly when rising water cuts off their escape routes.Sahni says livestock is not simply property for floodplain families, it is their livelihood. “People usually take their buffaloes with them on the roads. How will they earn? Now they have installed fencing around a small Yamuna pond here. How will buffaloes go there? They need to be there for survival. If a flood comes right now, there is no way we can rescue them immediately as there is only a small route to travel.”When asked who rescues stray animals during floods, he had no clear answer.PETA India told TOI that animals stranded during floods can face exhaustion, dehydration, hunger, injury and drowning, making rapid rescue and access to food, clean water and veterinary care critical.“The biggest challenge when trying to reach animals in emergency situations is getting to them in the first place. Access may be cut off by rising water, for instance,” said Sachin Bangera of PETA India.During last year’s floods, PETA India’s Rapid Response Team arranged a boat to rescue dogs stranded in flooded areas and at risk of drowning.“Animals who are left chained are the most vulnerable because they cannot escape, or they become exhausted and drown,” Bangera said.Aditi Bakshi, Animal Welfare Advocate and Specialist - Government and Public Policy at Mercy For Animals, says the problem goes deeper than rescue.“Many people are forced into an impossible choice by a system that gives them no option. Rescue boats and relief camps do not take animals. When the administration tells a family to evacuate and will not let them bring their cow, their pigs, or their two goats, the family has to choose between their children’s safety and the animal’s life.”She argues that flood preparedness must explicitly include animals.According to Bakshi, Delhi lacks a comprehensive operational framework covering animal evacuation, including a nodal officer, mapped animal shelters, pre-monsoon fodder stocks, evacuation protocols for large animals and regular drills. “A plan that has never been drilled is not a plan; it is a document,” she says.For Delhi’s floodplain residents, the Yamuna may rise for only a few days. The disruption can last months.That makes flood preparedness about far more than issuing warnings once the river begins to rise.“Relief must be immediate, but rehabilitation must be humane and sustainable. People should not have to repeatedly rebuild their lives every monsoon,” says Dr Heera Lal Patel, IAS.During a flood emergency, he says, authorities need to provide clear information, accessible evacuation routes, transport and safe shelters. Vulnerable families cannot be expected to organise an evacuation on their own.Rawat argues that Delhi needs scientifically determined, risk-based floodplain zoning.“The real measures of success are: how many people are taken out of high-risk locations, flood-storage capacity restored and new encroachment prevented.”For companion-animal guardians, PETA India recommends identifying safe locations where pets will be accepted, keeping an emergency kit ready, and ensuring animals are microchipped or wear collars with updated contact details.But the larger challenge is institutional.The Yamuna’s rise is predictable. The exact scale and timing of a flood may not be.For communities living beside the river, that distinction can mean the difference between having time to evacuate and scrambling for safety as the water arrives.And every September, Delhi faces the same question: when the Yamuna rises again, will the city be better prepared, or will thousands once again be forced to leave their lives behind?
Article Summary: A year after the Yamuna inundated large parts of Delhi, the river is again flowing above the danger mark. The immediate threat may be lower this time, but heavy rain in the upper catchment could quickly change the picture. The danger mark at the Old Iron Railway Bridge is 205.33 metres.

Article Title: Isro will never be privatised, its role won't be diminished: Space Agency & INSPACe chief

NEW DELHI/BENGALURU: Allaying the fears of some of its staff that the organisation will be privatised and its role reduced to an R&D lab, Isro Sunday dismissed “speculation” about any diminution of its role as “misinformation”.“These assertions are completely baseless and incorrect. We wish to categorically state that Isro will neither be privatised nor will its importance be diminished,” it said.Isro further said it would continue to remain “India’s principal institution for advanced space research and technology development, national and strategic missions, space science and exploration, and critical and frontier space capabilities”.Space promoter and regulator Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (INSPACe) chairperson Pawan Goenka also said Sunday that Isro would “remain the bedrock of the Indian space sector” and at the core of India’s space programme leading frontier research and the next generation of national missions like the space station and Gaganyaan.The agency said, “Participation of private sector in space is not about reducing its role.It is about enabling Isro to focus even more strongly on the next generation of India’s space programme, while industry scales mature technologies and capabilities. What is changing is not the importance of Isro, but the scale and structure of India’s space ecosystem. The transition is therefore towards an Isro-led national space ecosystem. ”The agency also said its role would progressively strengthen in areas where “its scientific expertise matters most: frontier R&D, advanced technologies, human spaceflight, next-generation launch systems, deep-space and planetary missions and strategic national capabilities. It will continue developing cutting-edge technologies, including advanced payloads for communication, navigation and Earth observation, sensors, propulsion systems and other critical technologies”.After nine Isro staff associations representing thousands sought clarification from the agency chairperson on the private sector shift, Goenka said on X, “Let me say it unequivocally: Isro’s role is by no means diminishing.”On scaling up the production of rockets and satellites in India, the INSPACe director declared that the country had set an “ambitious target” of 50 launches a year by 2030. “A goal of this scale cannot be achieved by one organisation alone. Govt and private industry have to build this future together,” he said.The INSPACe chairperson said, “The reforms since 2020 are about expanding India’s overall space ecosystem. IN-SPACe will facilitate and authorise greater non-govt participation, while NSIL will help commercialise mature capabilities.”Goenka said the idea of space reforms is to “let industry increasingly manufacture and scale mature launch vehicles, satellites and other systems, while Isro focuses on what it is uniquely placed to do: advanced R&D, scientific missions, strategic missions, new technologies, and infrastructure that is too complex for the private sector to develop on its own”.Assuring staff that they were going to handle big projects, he said, “Isro will remain at the core of India’s space programme, leading frontier research and the next generation of national missions, including Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035, an Indian crewed mission to the Moon by 2040, next-generation launch systems, and sustained lunar and planetary exploration.”“The direction is not a smaller Isro. It is a larger Indian space ecosystem, with Isro pushing the technological frontier,” he added.
Article Summary: Isro dismisses privatisation speculation, says role will only strengthen. Isro will remain at the core of India’s space programme, leading frontier research and the next generation of national missions. “A goal of this scale cannot be achieved by one organisation alone. Govt and private industry have to build this future together”

Article Title: What does the law say about inheritance? Know your rights
Article Text:
What can a daughter, wife, widow or mother legally claim?

Inheritance rights

Hindu women: Daughter has equal coparcenary rights

Muslim women: Share depends on the family structure

Christian women: Sons and daughters inherit equally

Parsi women: Daughter does not lose out to son

Legal steps to challenge a will

How can one challenge an unfair will

What if a woman is denied her share in property

What if the family says she has already given up her share

stridhan

So, what is a woman’s share in family property

For generations, inheritance in India has been shaped by family relationships, religious personal laws and the nature of the property being inherited.A daughter may have an equal right with her brother in one situation, but not necessarily in another. A widow may be entitled to a share in her husband's estate, while a woman may also own property in her own right through inheritance, gifts or other means.The biggest question often arises when a person dies without leaving a will. In such cases, known as intestate succession, the applicable law determines who inherits and in what proportion. The rules differ across religious communities.The Hindu Succession Act, 1956, governs succession among Hindus and also applies to Buddhists, Jains and Sikhs, subject to its provisions. Muslims are generally governed by Muslim personal law on intestate succession, while Christians and Parsis are principally covered by the Indian Succession Act, 1925.So what can a woman legally claim?One of the biggest changes to women's inheritance rights came with the Hindu Succession (Amendment) Act, 2005. It made a daughter a coparcener by birth in a Hindu joint family governed by Mitakshara law, giving her the same rights and liabilities as a son.The Supreme Court's 2020 judgment in Vineeta Sharma v Rakesh Sharma clarified that this right is acquired by birth and does not depend on whether the father was alive when the 2005 amendment came into force.Marriage also does not take away a daughter's coparcenary rights. However, an important distinction must be made between coparcenary property and a parent's self-acquired property.If a Hindu father dies intestate, leaving behind his wife, son and daughter, and the property is his self-acquired property, all three are Class I heirs. In a simple example involving property worth Rs 1 crore, the wife, son and daughter would each inherit about Rs 33.33 lakh.The calculation becomes more nuanced when the property is coparcenary property, explains advocate Rupali Jain.“If the Rs 1 crore is Mitakshara coparcenary property, the calculation is more nuanced. A notional partition is assumed immediately before the father's death. On the stated facts, assuming the father, one son and one daughter constitute the coparcenary and the wife is entitled to a share on such partition, the wife, son, daughter and father would each be attributed a one-fourth share, or Rs 25 lakh, for purposes of the hypothetical partition,” Jain said.The father's Rs 25 lakh share would then devolve equally among his Class I heirs, the wife, son and daughter. Each would receive an additional Rs 8.33 lakh. This means all three would ultimately receive approximately Rs 33.33 lakh.“The Supreme Court in Gurupad Khandappa Magdum v Hirabai Khandappa Magdum held that the fiction of notional partition must be carried through to its logical consequences and that the widow's share arising from the hypothetical partition cannot simply be ignored,” she added.Another common misconception is that every property owned by a parent is ancestral property in which children have a birthright. That is not necessarily so.Muslim inheritance in India operates under Muslim personal law, which does not follow the same joint-family property model.Islamic inheritance rules identify different categories of heirs and prescribe shares depending on which relatives survive the deceased. The applicable school of Muslim law can also matter.The daughter will generally receive half the son's share but the actual calculation depends on all the surviving heirs.A widow's share also depends on whether the deceased leaves descendants. Broadly, under commonly applied Sunni rules, a widow receives one-eighth where there are children or certain descendants and one-fourth where there are none."The share of a Muslim woman therefore has to be calculated based on the complete family structure," said advocate Pritish Sunil Teckchandani.Muslim testamentary succession is also different. Generally, a Muslim's power to make a will is restricted to one-third of the estate without the consent of the heirs, subject to applicable personal-law rules.For Christians, intestate succession is primarily governed by the Indian Succession Act, 1925.Where a Christian man dies without a will leaving a widow and children, the widow receives one-third of the estate, while the remaining two-thirds goes equally to the children.For example, if a Christian man dies leaving a wife, one son and one daughter and an estate worth Rs 90 lakh, each would ordinarily receive Rs 30 lakh. "The widow and each child would ordinarily receive one-third each," said Teckchandani.The position changes depending on which relatives survive the deceased, but there is no distinction between sons and daughters in the straightforward situation described above.Unlike Hindu law, Christian succession has no equivalent concept of coparcenary rights by birth. A Christian daughter does not become a co-owner of her father's property merely because she is his daughter; her inheritance generally arises upon succession.Parsi intestate succession is governed by special provisions in Part V of the Indian Succession Act. The exact entitlement depends on the relatives who survive the deceased.Thus, where a Parsi man dies intestate leaving a widow, son and daughter, the son and daughter inherit on an equal footing under the applicable rules.The calculation can change where there are more children, a predeceased child, grandchildren or other specified relatives.When a person dies without a valid will, the property does not automatically go to the eldest son or the closest male relative. The applicable succession law determines who inherits.For Hindus, the Hindu Succession Act lays down a hierarchy of heirs. A widow, son, daughter and mother are among the Class I heirs of a Hindu man who dies intestate.For Muslims, inheritance is calculated under applicable Muslim personal-law rules rather than a Class I heir system.For Christians and Parsis, the relevant provisions of the Indian Succession Act apply.This is why there is no single formula for a woman's inheritance in India. Her share can depend on her religion, relationship to the deceased, the relatives who survive, the nature of the property and whether there is a valid will.“For self-acquired property, a Hindu father can generally leave the entire property to his son and exclude his daughter through a valid Will. A daughter has no compulsory share in such property merely by virtue of being his daughter,” said Tekchandani.This is where the nature of the property becomes particularly important.A person can generally make a will determining how property that they legally own and can dispose of should be distributed. Therefore, a Hindu father can ordinarily leave his entire self-acquired property to his son and exclude his daughter."The daughter has no compulsory share in such property merely by virtue of being his daughter," said Teckchandani.But a will cannot simply wipe out another person's existing coparcenary interest. A daughter who already has a coparceny share cannot be deprived of that existing interest merely through her father's will."An unfair will is not necessarily an invalid will," explained Teckchandani. However, a woman can challenge a will if there are grounds to question its validity. These can include forgery, lack of testamentary capacity, coercion, undue influence, improper execution or other suspicious circumstances.Jain said courts may examine factors such as whether the testator was elderly, ill or dependent on the beneficiary, whether the beneficiary isolated the testator from other family members, whether there was a sudden departure from an earlier will, or whether the beneficiary was involved in preparing or executing the document."The person alleging coercion must produce credible evidence; mere suspicion or the fact that one child received substantially more property is generally insufficient," said Jain.Medical records, previous wills, messages, bank documents and testimony from doctors, neighbours, lawyers and attesting witnesses may become important evidence.The first step is to establish what the will says and what property it covers.A woman challenging a will should obtain the will, death certificate and relevant property documents. If probate or letters of administration proceedings are pending, she can enter the proceedings and raise objections."If probate proceedings are filed, enter appearance/file objections or a caveat, after which the proceeding becomes contentious," explained Jain.If no such proceedings are pending, the appropriate civil remedy will depend on the circumstances.The court can examine whether the will was properly executed and attested, whether the deceased had testamentary capacity and whether there was fraud, coercion, undue influence or another circumstance affecting its validity.The first step is to establish the property's ownership and character. Sale deeds, title documents, mutation records, partition deeds, gift or settlement deeds, wills and other records can help determine what a woman is actually entitled to.Depending on the dispute, a woman may approach a civil court seeking remedies such as partition and separate possession, declaration of rights, cancellation of an invalid document or an injunction.One of the biggest risks comes when family members ask a daughter to sign a release deed, relinquishment deed, family settlement, partition document or NOC without fully understanding its consequences."The biggest mistake is giving up legal rights informally in the name of maintaining family relations, without understanding the property's character or documenting the settlement," said Jain.A woman should determine whether the property is self-acquired, inherited or coparcenary, establish her legal share and obtain independent advice before signing away any interest.A daughter may be told that she has no claim because she is married, that her brother "needs the property", or that her share was already given to her through wedding expenses orWhether a woman has actually relinquished a property right depends on the applicable law and whether there is a legally valid document or transaction establishing that relinquishment."Family pressure can make people sign documents simply to avoid conflict, but such documents can have significant and sometimes irreversible consequences," said Teckchandani. A verbal family understanding and a legally valid relinquishment or settlement document are not necessarily the same thing.Well, there is no single answer to this question.For a Hindu woman, a daughter can have equal coparcenary rights with a son, while inheritance of self-acquired property after an intestate death follows a different calculation.For a Muslim woman, the share depends on the applicable personal law and the complete family structure. For Christian and Parsi women, succession is principally governed by the Indian Succession Act, with sons and daughters generally treated equally in the relevant intestate situations.A will can also change the outcome, particularly when it concerns property that the testator was free to dispose of. But a will that is unequal is not automatically invalid, nor can it simply extinguish an existing legal interest such as a coparcenary share.For women facing an inheritance dispute, the key questions are therefore: What personal law applies? Who survived the deceased? What kind of property is involved? Was there a valid will? Was the property already transferred or partitioned? And has the woman actually and legally relinquished her share?Knowing the answers to those questions is often the difference between walking away from property and successfully asserting a legal claim.
Article Summary: Inheritance in India has been shaped by family relationships, religious personal laws and the nature of the property being inherited. A widow may be entitled to a share in her husband's estate. A woman may also own property in her own right through inheritance, gifts or other means.

Article Title: Isro says its 'next chapter' is leading national space ecosystem
Article Text:
ISRO “would neither be privatised nor will its importance be diminished”.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Two days after nine employee bodies at Isro centres sought written clarity on the future role of the organisation amid space-sector reforms, Isro on Sunday hinted at its “next chapter” while categorically stating that it “would neither be privatised nor will its importance be diminished”.“Isro will continue to remain India’s principal institution for advanced space R&D, national and strategic missions, space science and exploration, and critical and frontier space capabilities. Participation of the private sector is not about reducing Isro’s role. It is about enabling Isro to focus even more strongly on the next generation of India’s space programme, while industry scales mature technologies and capabilities,” Isro said.Also read: Isro will remain ‘bedrock of Indian space sector’, says Goenka What is changing is not the importance of Isro, but the scale and structure of India’s space ecosystem, it said, adding that the space-sector reforms institutionalised through the Indian Space Policy 2023, along with progressive liberalisation of FDI policy, aim to create a larger, stronger and globally competitive Indian space ecosystem.“Industry, start-ups and academia are being enabled to participate across the space value chain, complementing and multiplying Isro’s capabilities.The reforms should therefore be seen as ecosystem expansion and capability multiplication, not privatisation,” Isro said.As India’s industrial and technological capabilities have grown, mature and scalable activities can increasingly be undertaken by Indian industry, it said, adding Isro has already transferred multiple technologies to industry.“Transferring a mature technology doesn’t mean Isro is withdrawing from that domain. It enables large-scale production, commercialisation, innovation and access to global markets while allowing Isro’s scientific and technical manpower to concentrate on advanced research, next-generation technologies and complex national missions,” It said.The transition is therefore towards an “Isro-led national space ecosystem.” “...Isro’s role will progressively strengthen in areas where its scientific expertise matters most: frontier R&D, advanced technologies, human spaceflight, next-generation launch systems, deep-space and planetary missions and strategic national capabilities,” it said.The agency added that it’ll continue developing cutting-edge technologies, including advanced payloads for communication, navigation and Earth observation, sensors, propulsion systems and other critical technologies.“Meanwhile, mature and routinely manufactured systems can increasingly be scaled through industry. Production of mature launch vehicles, routine satellites and other established systems can increasingly be undertaken by industry or PSUs through appropriate competitive processes,” Isro said.This, it says, allows Isro to devote more resources and scientific manpower to the next generation of technologies and missions, while the wider ecosystem provides the investment, manufacturing capacity and scale required by an expanding national space programme.Pointing out that the transition was important in the context of Space Vision 2047, it said technologies needed for establishing the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035, crewed mission to Moon by 2040, developing next-generation and reusable launch systems, pursuing sustained lunar and planetary exploration, and establishing India as a major global space power, require Isro to remain focused on advanced research and capabilities that cannot simply be substituted by commercial activity.The objective is “therefore to enable industry to scale mature capabilities while Isro pushes India towards the next technological frontier”.“The Department of Space provides overall policy direction, Isro remains the core organisation for advanced R&D, technology development and national missions. IN-SPACe facilitates and authorises the participation of non-government entities, while NSIL undertakes commercialisation and industry-led utilisation of mature capabilities,” Isro said.It added that industry and start-ups contribute investment, innovation, manufacturing capacity and market access. “At the same time, ownership and control of critical national space infrastructure and strategic capabilities will continue to remain with the Govt. Private participation in operations and services will be enabled where appropriate and will remain subject to national-security, safety and other regulatory requirements. Strategic and nationally critical capabilities will continue to be governed by security, safety, quality and national-interest considerations,” it said.
Article Summary: Isro has hinted at its ‘next chapter’ while categorically stating that it “would neither be privatised nor will its importance be diminished’ “Isro will continue to remain India’s principal institution for advanced space R&D, national and strategic missions, space science and exploration,” it said.

NEW DELHI: Faced with turmoil over the state leadership in Punjab, Congress has heaved a sigh of relief as politicians cutting across factional lines have welcomed Sachin Pilot 's appointment as party incharge of the poll-bound state in place of Bhupesh Baghel.Former Punjab chief minister Charanjit Channi and Lok Sabha MP Sukhjinder Randhawa, who lead the dissident group gunning for state president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, extended their best wishes to Pilot. Warring too has welcomed Pilot's appointment.While Channi expressed his "heartfelt thanks" to the Congress brass for "this important decision", Randhawa wished Pilot the "very best for this important responsibility" and said his experience, leadership and connect with the people will give new strength and momentum to the Congress organisation in the state.The duo's first reaction has assured the leadership that the decision on Pilot is in the right direction, though many believe coming days will decide if they are ready to move on from their demand for Warring's ejection. Sources said there is very little likelihood of a change in the state leadership now.Two months ago, Congress was shocked by the outbreak of dissidence in Punjab that goes to polls in February and where the ruling AAP has already launched its campaign for re-election.Congress had announced its election-related committees on July 1, but they have proved a non-starter as the appointments were followed by open groupism that brought the party activities to a halt.Now, Congress is hoping for a new start. NEW DELHI: The Centre is in a tangle over Supreme Court's landmark judgement on "creamy layer" that paved the way for induction in the elite civil services of OBC candidates who had cleared the examinations over past ten years but were denied appointments.On Aug 25, govt approached the apex court seeking clarification on the Rohit Nathan judgement that laid down that "salary" could not be added to the "income" to determine if a candidate from a PSU background falls in the "creamy layer" - like it is done for OBCs from non-PSU families. Govt, while seeking that it be allowed to go ahead with allocation of service for Civil Services-2025 without implementing the Nathan judgement, also raised questions about the SC's definition of "creamy layer".But barely a week ago, Centre told Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) that it intended to execute the SC order of March 11. "A decision has been made to implement the decision in terms of the judgement rendered by SC in Union of India vs Rohit Nathan," the ASG told the principal bench of CAT.On Aug 19, CAT was hearing a contempt petition against Centre as an OBC candidate, Basant Singh, had sought that the bench enforce its earlier order for his induction in civil services.His case was similar to those of candidates in whose favour SC delivered the Nathan judgement."It is further submitted by the learned ASG that 56 similarly placed candidates are also being considered along with the applicant," CAT quoted the ASG as submitting. CAT put off the case based on Centre's undertaking that necessary steps were being taken to implement the Nathan judgement.The apparently contradictory stands taken by govt within a week's interval have disappointed OBC candidates who felt the SC judgement in March had ended their wait for induction in civil services.The case pertains to department of personnel and training (DoPT)'s differential implementation of the "creamy layer" criterion for OBCs from a PSU background and others. While, as per 1993 office memorandum, "salary" and "agricultural income" are not included in computing the "income" of a family, DoPT has been taking "salary" into consideration for candidates with parents in PSUs. Govt has cited the absence of "equivalence of posts" - categorising posts in PSUs, banks, universities, etc.as "Group A, B, C, D" - as the source of confusion.But, according to guidelines, while Group A and Group B are ineligible for quotas, others are eligible if their "annual income" does not exceed Rs 8 lakh.After a long wait, following orders by three high courts in support of the candidates, SC ruled in March that "salary" cannot be the criterion for determination of "creamy layer" for any category as per the 1993 judgement and that candidates who have suffered should be inducted in civil services.
Article Summary: Centre in a tangle over Supreme Court's landmark judgement on "creamy layer" That paved the way for induction in the elite civil services of OBC candidates. Govt sought clarification on the Rohit Nathan judgement that laid down that "salary" could not be added to the "income"

Article Title: India, 163 others vote at UNGA for map with bigger Africa, shrunk North America

United Nations General Assembly voted Friday to adopt a new world map that makes the African continent bigger while shrinking North America and Europe, drawing ire from Washington.Aimed at "a more accurate representation" of continental landmasses, the resolution was supported by 164 countries, including India. US voted against it and six nations abstained.The new map, known as the Equal Earth cartographic projection, improves "the accuracy of the cartographic representation of the world", the resolution said. It urges member states to use the new map in place of the traditional Mercator projection.Foreign minister Robert Dussey of Togo, which sponsored the resolution, said maps "guide education, nourish imagination, and influence collective perceptions"."They are therefore never neutral; when they present a distorted image of our planet, they risk perpetuating inaccurate representation that is passed down through generations," he said.African Union Commission chair Mahmoud Ali Youssouf said, "Beyond cartography, this initiative underscores the importance of representing Africa on the basis of objective and scientifically established realities...Africa must be represented as it truly is: in its true dimensions and in its rightful place in the world."US, however, slammed the resolution, saying such moves are "the reason this institution is losing its credibility". Representative Yaryna Ferencevych said, "Instead of focusing on genuine problems... this body is debating map projects from the 16th century and their role in promoting reparations and cognitive justice."The Mercator projection was designed for maritime navigation by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator in 1569. It focused on depictions of the shapes and angles of land masses but their relative sizes were often inaccurate, largely due to the challenge of rendering a three-dimensional globe onto a two-dimensional map.It inflated northern regions and compressed equatorial ones, making Europe and North America appear much larger, while shrinking Africa and South America. Africa appears to be roughly as big as Greenland, though at 30.3 million sq km, it's about 14 times as large.France, which co-sponsored the resolution, announced Friday it would abandon the Mercator projection, in which "US, Russia and China take on a disproportionate visual prominence". Foreign minister Jean-Noel Barrot said, "Changing maps obviously doesn't change the world," "But correcting a distorted representation is already an act of truth."
Article Summary: The United Nations General Assembly voted Friday to adopt a new world map that makes the African continent bigger while shrinking North America and Europe. The resolution was supported by 164 countries, including India. US voted against it and six nations abstained. The new map, known as the Equal Earth cartographic projection, improves "the accuracy of the cartographic representation of the world"

NEW DELHI: Six people were killed and five were rescued after a five-storey boys' paying guest (PG) accommodation collapsed in southwest Delhi's Satya Niketan area on Sunday, officials said. Rescue operations were under way to search for any remaining people trapped under the rubble.The collapse involved a building known as 'Hostel Daze', which was being used as a boys' PG. An adjacent building also collapsed, according to eyewitnesses.JPN Apex Trauma Centre (AIIMS), on late Sunday, informed that it received 10 patients from the Satya Niketan building collapse. Four were brought dead, while one critically injured patient later succumbed. Three are admitted and undergoing treatment, one underwent limb surgery, and one with minor injuries was discharged after observation.The AIIMS Trauma Centre said eight injured people were brought to hospitals following the incident. Seven were taken to the AIIMS Trauma Centre, while one was admitted to Safdarjung Hospital. Two of those brought to AIIMS were declared brought dead.The death toll later rose to three, with authorities confirming that six people had been rescued from the rubble.Two National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams were deployed at the site, while two additional teams were kept on standby, NDRF Inspector General NS Bundela said. Rescue teams were working in coordination with the State Disaster Response Force, Delhi Fire Service and other agencies.The Delhi Fire Service received information about the collapse at around 1.30 pm, following which eight fire tenders and multiple rescue teams were rushed to the spot. Police also cordoned off the area as rescuers searched through the debris.Eyewitnesses said several students were believed to be inside the building when it collapsed. A local resident claimed the PG had around 15 rooms, with two to three students staying in each room, and that around 35 to 40 students were residing on its upper floors.Residents said many students were inside their rooms because it was Sunday. Several locals joined the rescue operation, removing debris with their hands and whatever tools were available.Residents alleged that construction or repair work was under way in the basement and that water had accumulated there. A local resident who has lived in the area for around two decades claimed the building's foundation was weak.Another resident said he had been inside the building shortly before the collapse and managed to get out minutes before the structure came down.The adjacent building was also reportedly leaning after the collapse, raising concerns about the safety of nearby structures.Residents said most students staying at the PG were from Kerala, Haryana and Uttar Pradesh and attended colleges including Motilal Nehru College, Atma Ram Sanatan Dharma College and Sri Venkateswara College.One resident said students were paying around Rs 12,000 per bed at the accommodation. Residents also raised concerns about the condition of buildings in the congested locality, where several residential properties have reportedly been converted into student PG accommodations.Delhi Chief Minister Rekha Gupta visited the site and reviewed the ongoing search and rescue operation. Emergency teams continued clearing the rubble and searching for anyone who may still be trapped."No one will be spared," she says.The Rekha Gupta-led Delhi government has ordered a magisterial inquiry into the incident and directed that an FIR be registered against the building owner, the chief minister’s office (CMO) said.The decision was taken following an on-site review and a preliminary assessment of the incident, the CMO said.“Following an on-site review and based on the preliminary assessment, the chief minister has ordered a Magisterial Inquiry of the incident and an FIR against the building owner,” the CMO said.It added that those found responsible for the incident would be held fully accountable and face the strictest provisions of the law.Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed condolences over the deaths in the Satya Niketan building collapse and prayed for the speedy recovery of those injured. He said authorities were working at the site and assisting people affected by the incident.

NEW DELHI: New Delhi: With vultures vanishing from nearly 72% of their historically known nesting sites across India over the years, Union environment minister Bhupender Yadav on Sunday pitched for conservation of the nature’s most efficient scavengers and called for continued efforts to create Vulture Safe Zones.He said vulture-safe veterinary practices, safe food availability and technical capacity-building were needed to aid species recovery in the wild.Speaking at an International Vulture Awareness Day 2026 event in Panchkula, Haryana, Yadav urged veterinary professionals, livestock owners, local administrations and communities to support conservation and safe carcass-management practices.Vultures play a vital role in keeping ecosystems clean by feeding on decaying carcasses. Unlike predators, they rarely kill their own prey. Instead, they are scavengers that feed on carrion left behind by other animals. By removing dead animal matter, vultures help keep the environment clean and significantly reduce the risk of disease spreading.Vulture populations have fallen sharply since the 1990s, mainly because of disruption to their food chain and veterinary use of diclofenac, an anti-inflammatory drug commonly administered to livestock.Research found vultures feeding on carcasses of treated livestock suffered kidney failure and died.India has nine vulture species: white-rumped, long-billed, slender-billed, red-headed, Egyptian, Himalayan griffon, Eurasian griffon, cinereous and bearded vultures. They are found from the Himalayan range to Kerala.A pan-India assessment by Wildlife Institute of India scientists last year recorded only 120 active historical nesting sites among 425 documented in literature across 25 states. Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan accounted for about 63% of all vulture nests. Researchers also identified 93 new nesting locations, taking the total to 213, including 103 in protected areas.Conservation breeding of vultures is under way at centres in Pinjore, Haryana; Rajabha Khawa, West Bengal; and Rani, Assam.During 2025–26, Jatayu Conservation Breeding Centre in Pinjore housed 356 vultures, bred 35 chicks and released or contributed 87 birds for reintroduction, environment ministry said. It transferred 90 birds to other conservation-breeding institutions and trained 1,222 participants from 22 institutions.The centre, run jointly by Haryana Forest Department and Bombay Natural History Society, breeds white-rumped, long-billed and slender-billed vultures.

Bathinda, Punjab's sports event, 'Khedan Wattan Punjab Diyan-2026', began on Saturday, with Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann setting a vision of taking the state's sporting talent to the global stage.The fourth season will bring nearly 10 lakh players aged 14 to over 70 years into 39 sporting disciplines, including four para-sports.The event, which kicked off in Bathinda, will conclude in Patiala on November 29, with Rs 12.50 crore in prize money for winners, including cash awards for veteran players for the first time, according to an official statement.On the occasion, Mann also honoured Commonwealth Games-2026 silver medallists Harjinder Kaur and Lovepreet Singh with Rs 50 lakh each.The opening ceremony of the fourth season of the Games featured several performances, including Bhangra and Giddha. NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Sunday said the Narendra Modi government has prepared a roadmap to make India drug-free by 2029, calling the fight against narcotics a national security priority.Addressing the media, Shah stated that the fight against narcotics has moved beyond isolated actions to become a coordinated national campaign.Shah said it was PM Modi’s objective that “drug-free youth power” would lead India towards Viksit Bharat by 2047. He said the government was committed to tackling narcotics with the same approach it used against Naxalism and terrorism.“Before 2014, the fight against narcotics was largely conducted in small units and isolation,” Shah said, adding that agencies had often focused on catching small-time accused. The government, he said, had now made the anti-narcotics fight a national security priority.Detailing the approach Shah stated that the government has strengthened its anti-narcotics drive through NCORD, state anti-narcotics task forces and joint coordination between agencies, along with the MANAS helpline and a revamped NCB. It also created the NIDAN database of narcotics offenders and a nationwide data-driven map of drug hotspots and trafficking patterns.The government now uses a “bottom-to-top” and “top-to-bottom” reverse investigation model, tracing small drug seizures back to their source and large consignments forward to their intended users to uncover the wider network.Shah also highlighted the government’s claims on internal security, saying terrorism in Jammu and Kashmir was declining and the sentiment of separatism had weakened since the abrogation of Article 370.He said those who had envisioned a Maoist “red corridor” from Tirupati to Pashupati had laid down arms and joined the mainstream, while more than 10,000 youths in the northeast had also surrendered their arms.Shah said Naxalism, which had persisted for five decades, had become a thing of the past. “We have eradicated Naxalism and will deal with menace of narcotics in the same manner,” he asserted.

Article Title: IIT Mandi orders inquiry after poster says Shudras should ‘serve higher classes’
Article Text:

What the controversial poster said

Behera's Gita and ISKCON links
