NEW DELHI: IIT Mandi has set up an inquiry after a Bhagavad Gita-themed poster displayed on its campus during Janmashtami celebrations described Shudras as being meant to "serve higher classes", triggering controversy over caste discrimination.Institute Director Laxmidhar Behera said the poster was part of a student-led event and had not been approved by the institute. He said he was "shocked" when he learnt about the display and stressed that IIT Mandi does not support caste-based discrimination.In an email to the IIT Mandi community on Sunday, Behera described the development as an "Outright condemnation of recent poster display within campus". He said the poster, displayed on September 4, had not been endorsed by the institute "in any manner"."I have personally fought against caste-based discrimination in any form in every forum. I have instituted an enquiry committee in this matter such that the institute campus is never used for any such violation of social harmony. I fully empathise with members of our community who have been hurt by this incident," he wrote.Behera said IIT Mandi was committed to "the values of equality, social justice, scientific temper" and the principles laid down in the Constitution."The institute strongly condemns any form of caste based discrimination," he said, urging members of the campus community to "stand together against such biases/discrimination in any form".Speaking to PTI, Behera said the poster had been prepared for a student event. He said the inquiry committee included faculty members and representatives from different social categories, including members of the Scheduled Castes and Other Backward Classes.The poster, titled "Bhagavad Gita - The Timeless Wisdom", was put up outside the institute's auditorium during Janmashtami celebrations.It divided society into four groups mentioned in the Bhagavad Gita, namely Brahmanas, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas and Shudras. It described Brahmanas as those who "spread God's message", Kshatriyas as those who "protect society and spirituality" and Vaishyas as those who "drive economy, support others".For Shudras, however, the poster listed their role as "serve higher classes", which became the focus of the controversy.The poster also quoted a Bhagavad Gita verse stating that the four divisions of human society were created according to the "three modes of material nature and the work associated with them".Behera said he had been away from IIT Mandi and returned on Saturday. He said he learnt about the controversy on Sunday morning."I have not seen the poster. I don't want to take a side here and let the panel decide," he told PTI.The controversy has also drawn attention to Behera's long association with the Bhagavad Gita and ISKCON.According to his official IIT Mandi profile, Behera has spent 27 years teaching what he describes as the "universal principles of peace through Bhagavad Gita". He is also known as "HG Lila Purushottam Das" and is the founder of the proposed Bhaktivedanta University, whose website describes it as an ISKCON initiative.Behera currently teaches a three-credit course on the Bhagavad Gita at IIT Mandi.He defended ISKCON's position on caste, saying the organisation opposes discrimination and promotes equality."ISKCON is the only organisation that strictly and strongly speaks against caste-based discrimination. In ISKCON, pujaris are also from the Shudra community. Muslims are also pujaris," he claimed."We are against casteism in all forms. All occupational duties are according to guna and karma," he added.Behera also highlighted what he said was increased representation of marginalised communities at IIT Mandi during his tenure. According to him, the institute had no OBC, SC or ST faculty members when he joined, while their numbers have since risen substantially. The IIT director has previously faced criticism over his public views.In 2023, he asked students to take a pledge against eating meat and linked landslides and cloudbursts in Himachal Pradesh to cruelty towards animals. In 2022, shortly after becoming IIT Mandi director, a video surfaced in which he claimed to have helped a friend's family get rid of "evil spirits" through chanting holy mantras.More recently, IIT Mandi's Indian Knowledge System and Mental Health Applications Centre held a conference in June that included sessions on the Bhagavad Gita, Ayurveda and reincarnation. Behera was among its general chairs and co-organised a session titled "Reincarnation, OBEs and afterlife communication".The institute's inquiry committee will now examine how the poster was prepared, displayed and presented during the student-led event.
Article Summary: IIT Mandi sets up inquiry after Bhagavad Gita-themed poster sparks controversy. Poster described Shudras as being meant to "serve higher classes" Institute Director Laxmidhar Behera said the poster was part of a student-led event. He said he was "shocked" when he learnt about the display and stressed that IITMandi does not support caste-based discrimination.

NEW DELHI: Former Chief Election Commissioner SY Quraishi on Sunday criticised the Election Commission over its special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, claiming that the exercise had effectively removed around 14-15 crore people from the country's voter lists.Speaking to news agency ANI, Quraishi urged the poll panel to disclose the number of voters deleted, describing the exercise as a "great success" in achieving something the National Population Commission could not."I would like to compliment the Election Commission for completing a very difficult mission of eliminating about 14-15 crore population of India through this exercise. I don't know how many illegal immigrants they have found, which was the main purpose of this exercise. It's a pity they have not disclosed this figure," Quraishi said."I would request them to please come out with this figure, so that we know what a great success you have been, and also that you have achieved something that the National Population Commission could not do. You have contributed a lot to population control by eliminating about 15% of India's population," he added.Quraishi also questioned the intent behind the SIR exercise, arguing that voting is a constitutional right and not something to be granted by the Election Commission."I think the entire SIR exercise is not well-intentioned. The way it has deleted crores of voters is tinkering with democracy. You are a citizen of India. I'm a citizen of India. Voting is our constitutional right," he said."Article 326 says that everyone shall be registered. So it is not a charity from the Election Commission that they will give you that," he added.The Election Commission is conducting the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls in several states to ensure that voter lists are accurate, updated and free of ineligible or duplicate entries, while ensuring that no eligible voter is left out.The nationwide SIR was announced in October 2025 by Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. The poll panel cited migration, voters being registered at multiple places, failure to remove deceased voters and the inclusion of foreign nationals in electoral rolls as factors behind the exercise.The revision has since been rolled out across several states and Union territories, including those heading into elections. The exercise has drawn sustained criticism from opposition parties.In Maharashtra, the SIR came under scrutiny after the draft electoral roll showed around two crore fewer voters than the previous roll.According to data released by Maharashtra's Chief Electoral Officer, 7,71,65,562 of the state's 9,78,54,049 electors had submitted their enumeration forms as of August 17.

She later called him and said that she was feeling unwell and intended to consult a doctor.When the doctor was reportedly unavailable, Devi began making her way back. At some point, she apparently got onto a motorcycle.Lal said he subsequently received a call from a person who was accompanying his daughter. The person told him that Devi had run towards the river.The development prompted Lal to speak to his daughter over the phone. He said he repeatedly asked her what had happened and whether somebody had said or done anything to her.Lal recalled Devi telling him, "Nobody should come near me."He continued trying to understand what had happened and urged her to explain why she was behaving that way.According to Lal, Devi responded, "No, papa. NEW DELHI: India and China are set to hold the first Corps Commander-level talks in the eastern sector on Sunday, with military officers from both sides meeting at the Wacha-Damai border meeting point in Arunachal Pradesh amid unresolved issues along the Line of Actual Control (LAC), ANI reported citing sources.The meeting, scheduled for September 6, is expected to provide a platform to address the ongoing issues in the area. The talks will be held at Wacha on the Indian side, with India represented by 3 Corps Commander Lt Gen Girish Kalia, according to the report by ANI.The Indian Army's 3 Corps, based at Rangapahar, and 4 Corps, headquartered in Tezpur, are responsible for the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh.India and China have differing perceptions of the LAC, which has periodically led to face-offs and other issues on the ground. Doval and Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi discussed maintaining peace and tranquillity along the border and advancing bilateral ties.The engagement is part of a gradual improvement in India-China relations following a series of high-level meetings between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping. The two leaders have stressed that India and China are development partners rather than rivals and that differences should not be allowed to become disputes.Recently, Army Chief Gen Dhiraj Seth also visited the 3 Corps headquarters, where he was briefed on operational readiness and measures to strengthen the formation's combat capabilities.

India emerges as key diesel supplier to Europe

India supplied about 60 per cent of the diesel transiting through the Bab-el-Mandeb towards Europe in August, strengthening its role as a key source of refined fuel as Russian exports remain depressed and US shipments begin to decline, according to a report.Around 2,00,000 barrels per day of diesel, or gasoil, crossed the strategic shipping route for Europe last month, close to year-earlier levels after flows nearly stalled in March and April. Indian refiners accounted for roughly 60 per cent of that volume, energy analytics firm Vortexa said in a report.India, the world’s fourth-largest refiner, has 258.1 million tonnes per annum of installed capacity, above domestic fuel demand. It exported 61.5 million tonnes of petroleum products in 2025-26, making it a major global supplier, PTI reported.However, sustaining these flows could become difficult. India’s crude and condensate imports fell to about 3.8 million barrels per day in August from 4.8 million barrels per day a year earlier, data showed.Russian diesel exports averaged only around 1,50,000 barrels per day during the first 25 days of August, down about 6,10,000 barrels per day year-on-year and 81 per cent below the five-year seasonal average.The scheduled easing of Russia’s diesel export ban from September 1 may not quickly restore supplies, with Ukrainian drone strikes continuing to disrupt refineries and export infrastructure. Vortexa recorded 32 refinery attacks across July and August.The Perm refinery, with capacity of 2,60,000 barrels per day, was left operating at only about 28 per cent of its crude distillation capacity after an attack, while no diesel cargoes have left Tuapse since a May strike.The US supplied about half of Europe’s seaborne diesel imports from outside the region in August, at around 5,20,000 barrels per day. But shipments fell from nearly 5,40,000 barrels per day in the first half of August to about 3,50,000 barrels per day in the second half.
Article Summary: India supplied about 60 per cent of the diesel transiting through the Bab-el- Mandeb towards Europe in August. Russian exports remain depressed and US shipments begin to decline. India, the world’s fourth-largest refiner, has 258.1 million tonnes of installed capacity.

Sikkim, September 6: A landslide occurred above the Chyakoong River in Sikkim’s Mangan district during the intervening night of September 5 and 6, authorities said.The district administration received reports from the district police and Chungthang Sub-Division police about the incident near OC Bhir. Article Summary: A landslide occurred above the Chyakoong River in Sikkim’s Mangan district during the intervening night of September 5 and 6. A large section of the hillside along a newly constructed road cutting of the Naga-Tosa Road collapsed near the confluence of the Teesta and ChYakoong rivers, opposite the Theng Tunnel. The Teesta River is currently flowing normally, although water has accumulated in both rivers. Water continues to flow through both rivers despite the accumulation.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday shared a video of his interaction with three students who were injured during police action amid recent student protests in Bihar.The three were part of a group of students from Bihar who met the Lok Sabha leader of opposition at his Delhi residence on September 3. In a social media post, Gandhi said the three students had been “shot at”, referring to a protest in Siwan, Bihar, on July 25.“Think about it: what crime had these children committed that they were shot? They had asked the government for just three things — education, employment, and accountability,” the Raebareli MP wrote on X.The leg bone of one of the students, he added, was shattered after he was hit by a bullet fired from an AK-47.“Along with it, his dream of joining the Army and serving the country was shattered too. Bullets tore through the shoulders of two other students,” Rahul Gandhi wrote.“They were not criminals. They were children from poor families who had gone out to study carrying the dreams of their families — some wanted a good job, while others wanted to change the circumstances of their homes,” he added.The Congress leader further remarked that while their physical wounds would heal, there is no answer to how the psychological trauma they had suffered could be treated."Mr prime minister, Mr chief minister — their broken bones will heal. Can you give them back their broken dreams?" Rahul Gandhi said, questioning Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Bihar chief minister Samrat Choudhary.Several parts of Bihar witnessed student protests, some of which turned violent, on July 25 as part of a broader agitation by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in Delhi. The CJP was leading protests demanding the resignation of then-Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak issue, along with reforms in the education system.The CJP, which had been protesting at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar since June 21, called off its agitation on July 25, shortly after Pradhan resigned. Union minister Pralhad Joshi has since been given additional charge of the Education ministry.The Bihar government has told the Supreme Court that a police constable fired four rounds from an AK-47 into the air after being trapped in a crowd, while maintaining that no protester was injured in the firing. The constable has since been suspended.

NEW DELHI: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge on Sunday launched a sharp attack on Prime Minister Narendra Modi and accused him of turning his address at Delhi University 's SRCC into "yet another political campaign" instead of facing questions from the youth.In a social media post on X, Kharge also attacked PM Modi for giving the opposition "a new adjective every" year, calling it his "modus operandi" to hide his own failures."Modi ji visited Delhi University's SRCC yesterday. It was an opportunity to engage with the country's youth and discuss education and their future. But unfortunately, instead of facing questions from the youth, the speech once again turned into a political campaign," Kharge said."In a democracy, to suppress questions, giving the opposition a new adjective every year, so that their own failures remain hidden! Naraz Fufa, Dimaagi Naxal, Urban Naxal, Khan Market Gang, Andolan-jiwi, Parjivi. Adjectives keep changing, but the Modi government's anti-people policies do not change," he added.Kharge also advised PM Modi to listen to the voices of students, saying that "solutions won't come from beating around the bush.""Modi ji, outreach is only needed when you become out of reach," Kharge said."The Prime Minister showed his 'report card'. The country's youth is also standing up with its report card. Listen to Chhatron Ki Goonj, solutions won't come from beating around the bush!!" he added.This comes a day after PM Modi took a jibe at Congress, describing its student outreach campaign, "Chhatron Ki Goonj", as "jhooth ki goonj".Addressing the centenary celebrations of Delhi University's Shri Ram College of Commerce (SRCC), PM Modi said, "...Main jaanta hoon, sach ki Hunkkaar ke aage jhooth ki goonj tik nahi sakegi (I know that the echo of lies cannot stand before the roar of truth)."PM Modi also described those who oppose government initiatives as "Naraz Fufa"."But outside this campus, you will encounter a new world. You will meet two kinds of people. One kind consists of people who positively transform the strength of society into the strength of the nation. The second kind is made up of people who become the 'Naraz Fufa' whenever any work is started," he said.
Article Summary: Mallikarjun Kharge accuses PM Modi of turning his address into "yet another political campaign" Kharge also attacked PM Modi for giving the opposition "a new adjective every" year. This comes a day after PM Modi took a jibe at Congress, describing its student outreach campaign as "jhooth ki goonj"
